item.title: Lindsay Clancy case shines spotlight on postpartum psychosis
item.description:
The high-profile murder trial of Lindsay Clancy — which ended in a mistrial last week after a jury was unable to convict or acquit the Massachusetts mother in the 2023 strangling deaths of her three young children — put a renewed spotlight on postpartum psychosis, the severe psychiatric condition her lawyers say she was suffering from at the time. As attention moves on from the trial, some researchers want more concrete changes that could improve how postpartum psychosis is researched, treated and prevented. How that happens — and how quickly — is unclear. While some in the mental health community applaud the improvements in how postpartum psychosis is recognized, others think the condition needs a more formal diagnosis for better long-term research. item.title: The Supreme Law Without 9/11
item.description:
In my new Civitas Essay, I discussed how our present legal order stems from the events of 9/11. Here, I will spin out a counterfactual: what would the legal order in 2026 look like if the terrorist attacks of 2001 had never happened? This compressed thought experiment will elucidate to the modern generation how significant 9/11 was to the very issues that define the Supreme Court today. Counterfactuals are just that–--contrary to fact. Take everything I write here with two towers of salt. Imagine that September 11, 2001 was a date like any other. Perhaps the dots were connected and the terrorist attacks were foiled. Or perhaps the plan fell apart when Saudi nationals were only interested in piloting jumbo jets and not landing them.
